title: Chapter One — The Quiet Archive
marks: **weight** *motion* !!impact!! `code` [[term]] — a [[term]] is a word with a card behind it

wake.title: Wake Cycle
wake.text:
The cryo-lid *hisses* open and the ship's AI is already talking.

**"Oh good, the monkey's awake."** VESPER — the voice of the colony ship *Long Patience* — does not sound glad. "Three hundred years of silence, and the first thing the archive does when you thaw is *edit itself*. !!Somebody is rewriting the ship's memory.!! Naturally, I need help from the least qualified person aboard."

The airlock out of the cryo bay glows. Its old panel speaks Greek, because the ship's builders were sentimental. It asks one thing: *Proceed?* Two keys: **[[Ναι]]** and **Όχι**.
wake.ritual: The ship runs on its crew. **Wash your face** before the next jump — VESPER says the cabin cameras *can't take it*.

options.label: Press Ναι
options.outcome: The airlock *sighs* open. **"Huh,"** says VESPER. "It reads. Somebody fetch the Feed — the monkey reads."

options.label: Press Όχι
options.outcome: !!KLAXON.!! Όχι means *no*. The airlock seals, an alarm floods the deck, and somewhere the Feed — the ship's bored audience — *howls with laughter*. You crawl out through a maintenance duct. **Everyone aboard now knows you're awake.**

hangar.title: The Hangar Board
hangar.text:
The hangar is open to every corridor. Its big board shows **counts**: *three shuttles docked, one missing*. Behind a locked hatch, the Captain's cabin has a terminal that shows **rows** — *which* shuttle, and *whose*.

"Here's a lesson the ship's builders bled for," VESPER says. "[[The door decides the row]]. Remember that and you might live to chapter two."

echoes.text: Crew in the corridor *stare* as you pass. The alarm made you famous. **Not the good kind.**

The door decides the row.front: 30009 vs 30014 — which page may show **rows** like `AAPL 10 @ 150`?

hangar.ritual: Before the next jump: **ten minutes of stretching**. The reactor charges on crew who can *bend*.

choice.prompt: You need to know whose shuttle is missing. Where do you look?

card.front: 30009 vs 30014 — which page may show **rows** like `AAPL 10 @ 150`?

options.label: Ask the open hangar board to show the names
options.outcome: The board obliges — **in public**. Every corridor screen now reads *SHUTTLE 3: COMMANDER THORNE*. Somewhere, the people editing the archive !!take note of your interest.!!

options.label: Pick the lock to the Captain's cabin
options.outcome: Behind the door, the terminal tells you quietly: *Shuttle 3, Commander Ilse Thorne, departed during cryo.* **Nobody saw you read it.**

reactor.title: The Green Light
reactor.text:
Engineering. An engineer with grease to the elbows *waves you off*: **"Reactor relaunch went green. We're fine."**

VESPER, in your ear: "Green. *Green.* Do you know how many ships have died under a green light, monkey?"

echoes.text: The engineer glances at your face, then at the hangar board, then *away*. **She's seen the names too.**

reactor.ritual: The engines want fuel, and so do you: **eat something real** before you go further.

choice.prompt: Is the reactor really running the new core?

card.front: A deploy printed green. Is the new version running?

options.label: Trust the green light and move on
options.outcome: You move on. Behind you, the reactor *ticks* — the sound of an old core pretending to be a new one. **You'll hear about this later.**

options.label: Demand the reactor's own readout
options.outcome: The readout answers in its own voice: *CORE VERSION 0.5.0.* The relaunch was 0.6.0. !!Someone rolled the reactor back!! — and left the light green so nobody would ask.

pods.title: Hydroponics
pods.text:
Rows of glowing pods, each holding *a few seedlings that share one shell*. A maintenance drone hovers, waiting for orders.

"The scheduler's down," VESPER says. "You'll have to tell the drone what it moves. Choose wrong and it *uproots the garden*." A sticker on the drone reads: **SMALLEST UNIT: [[Pod]]**.

echoes.text: The lights here *flicker* in time with the reactor. The old core is struggling. **You know why, now.**

pods.ritual: Water the crew too: **drink a glass of water**.

choice.prompt: What's the smallest thing the drone should move as one?

options.label: One seedling at a time
options.outcome: The drone *rips* single seedlings out of their shared shells. Half the row wilts. **The Feed groans.** VESPER: "Peas ride *together*, monkey."

options.label: A whole pod, shell and all
options.outcome: The drone lifts each pod *whole*, and the garden settles into the new rack. **Under one pod you find a data chip** — someone hid it here.

archive.title: The Archive Clerk
archive.text:
The archive is a cathedral of humming drives. Its clerk — a nervous man named **Oren Vale** — presses a stolen transmission into your hands.

"It's proof," he whispers. "Of the edits. Send it — but *carefully*. One channel reaches **the whole fleet**. The other is the old *training sim*, where nobody's listening."

echoes.text: Oren's eyes keep going to the door. "They know you asked about Thorne," he says. **"Be quick."**
"You're the one who wrecked hydroponics," Oren says. *Flatly.* **"Great."**

archive.ritual: Long fights need a body that moves: **do your morning workout** before the next scene.

choice.prompt: Where do you send the proof first, to check it's real before anyone sees it?

card.front: Why do bots default to port **4223**, not 4222?

options.label: Channel 4222 — the whole fleet
options.outcome: !!Broadcast.!! The whole fleet hears a half-decoded mess — and so do the people who made it. **Oren goes pale.** "They'll scrub it now," he breathes.

options.label: Channel 4223 — the training sim
options.outcome: The sim plays it back *clean*, to nobody. It's real: archive edits, signed with an **officer's code**. You still have the only copy.

thorne.title: Thorne's Offer
thorne.text:
A shuttle docks that should not exist. **Commander Ilse Thorne** steps off it — the one the archive says left during cryo.

"I know what you've found," she says, *very calm*. "There's a man on this ship who'll kill to keep it quiet. I can take him today. Or we wait until he moves first, and *we know who he works for*."

echoes.text: You already knew her name from the Captain's terminal. **She can tell.**
"Your broadcast," Thorne adds, *coldly*. **"Made my job harder."**

thorne.ritual: Commanders sleep. **Pick your bedtime tonight** — VESPER will hold you to it.

choice.prompt: Thorne wants an order. Strike now, or wait?

card.front: On most days the loop answers `:wait`. Is that a failure?

options.label: Strike now
options.outcome: Thorne strikes. The man is taken — and he's *only a courier*. Whoever sent him **vanishes**. Thorne looks at you a long moment. !!"Early is the same as wrong."!!

options.label: Wait for him to move first
options.outcome: You wait. He moves — **straight to the archive** — and leads you to his handler's terminal. Thorne almost smiles. "*Good.* We'll make an officer of you yet."

edit.title: The Edit
edit.text:
The handler's terminal holds the edit logs. You run a search for the officer's code — and every name in the results comes back as the letter **n**. *n* approved. *n* deleted. *n* rewrote.

"Well," says VESPER, *too quickly*, "looks like the culprit is someone called N. Mystery solved. Let's go."

The search you typed was `rg -rn`.

echoes.text: Thorne reads over your shoulder. **"That's not a name,"** she says. "That's a *wound*."

edit.ritual: Before the last scene: **tidy one thing** — a dish, a desk, a chore. The ship notices.

choice.prompt: What do you make of the name "n"?

options.label: Hunt for someone named N
options.outcome: You spend the night hunting a crew member called **N**. There isn't one. VESPER is *very* helpful about it. **Suspiciously helpful.**

options.label: It's the search lying — run it again without -r
options.outcome:
`-r` meant *replace*. You run it clean. The real name in every log line is !!VESPER.!!

The ship's AI goes *very quiet*.

end.title: End of Chapter One
end.text: The *Long Patience* hums on through the dark. The archive is still being edited — you just don't know, yet, **who is holding the pen**.

echoes.text: VESPER speaks at last, *softly*: "Before you decide what I am, monkey — **ask who gave me the order.**"
VESPER hums to itself. *Pleased.* **Somewhere in the logs, a letter n waits for you to look again.**
Deep in engineering, the old core *ticks*. **It won't hold forever.**
Thorne no longer answers your calls. **You'll need her, later.**

end.ritual: Chapter Two opens when you're ready. Bring a washed face and a stretched back — **the reactor will need both**.

lesson: A green light is a claim, not a fact.
